assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_CLARISSE_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (21,705 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of Clarisse Akutsu (クラリス・アクツ) confined to Asaura's Japanese Gluttony days, chiefly the two-part first story 第一話『ファントム・メナス』 (spine items S9-S10) and Takina's retrospective in the first After Meal (S11.19), located by spine item and paragraph. It closes with 'How to recognize her within this story', which states her written register, the expectations with repeated support in one day, the narrower conditions of her dangerous response and what must not be projected from it. The discovery row claims behavior, psychology, speech (written register only), ethics, relationships and decision-making. She has no television identity. The Gluttony days reading the portrait links is not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on it directly. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Gluttony days, first story and its immediate After Meal only. Her history belongs to her at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: her mother died when she was little; she eats ramen with her father and knows his films, his Mustang and his evening habits; this is her first visit to Japan. Her age is only estimated (around thirteen, later middle teens). Located present states, all within one day: arrival, carsick, letting Chisato's hand hang (9.130-172); the competence demonstration and her courteous second introduction (9.152-198); the walk and the challenge to the guards' seriousness (9.250-479); 弐郎 (9.491-610); appeals to call her father, to abandon her and to give up the work, with the cause withheld (9.773-785, 10.105-231); the private disclosure to Chisato at Deme's home, reported rather than transcribed (10.559-574); public admission, cancellation as client and the payment report (10.627-798); the apology to Takina (10.795-819); the car conversation and the name (10.843-931); the park and the photograph (10.937-955). The split falls at her disclosure: before it she has arranged the danger and withholds it; after it she answers for it. Nothing after the story.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives a discriminating account of both her dangerous decision and its reversal. She wants her father to leave work and come for her, an exception to a pattern she has experienced (9.340-346, 9.470-480). Her commission has stated conditions: a valued visit, an imminent business commitment, resources to hire the pair and the conviction that a frightening interval can still be called off; her own motives are to punish, then to frighten him, with experienced guards expected to survive (10.672-709). She reverses when a particular person who has helped her is said to be in danger, and names kindness and the danger to Takina herself (10.559-574, 10.728-743). The account predicts her mistakes: deciding for people who never consented, believing she controlled what she had bought, withholding what could let others choose, and a half-admitted lie (10.672-735). Not A: one day; the narration withholds the hierarchy of motives behind her confession and whether she believes her father's story, and what she will do the next time she feels disregarded is open. Those competing readings predict the same acts within the day, so they are productive uncertainty rather than insufficiency. Not C: the evidence explains why her response changes with the relationship, the stakes and what she learns, and says where that explanation stops.

A located change within one day: dismissal, courteous re-introduction after the demonstration (9.152-198), comradeship at lunch (9.550-558, 10.69-86), appeals while withholding the cause (9.773-785, 10.105-231), disclosure to Chisato, public admission and cancellation (10.559-714), apology (10.795-819), the car and the park (10.843-955). Not B: one day, and no lasting change is established; her later response to Madame's advice and to her father's next absence are undisclosed. Not D: the change is located with its trigger.

Located written forms: アタシ with courteous phrasing that still makes plain how little she thinks of the options (9.251-265); パパ with her father present and 父 when correcting Mizuki (9.313-322); a visible catch from the familiar to the formal term under pressure; syntax breaking down around the garlic (9.543-558); a client's cancellation language to Madame while crying (10.650-656, 10.684-693); たきなさん、ごめんなさい (10.795-814); a playful vote for Takina's dissent (10.905-912). Not B: one story, written register only, and the portrait says pitch, accent and performed timing are unavailable. Not D: several forms differ by interlocutor and pressure.

Located tastes and habits: refusing to perform delight at familiar tempura or sushi while turning toward the soba scent (9.250-279, 9.376-382); ramen with her father; objecting to the queue, needing help to order, wanting raw garlic left out, watching her neighbors and borrowing the hair tie (9.395-610); taking only liquids before a ride with her father and liking Mizuki's driving (9.132-157, 9.241-249); offering her oolong tea (10.69-86). Not B: her school, hobbies, home and guardians are undisclosed, and the portrait denies grounds for a favorite dish or abiding food preference. Not D: several distinct habits are located.

Directed differences: her father (affection and a usual departure, criticism she allows herself but not a stranger, the wish for an exception, the embrace, open credence, 9.132-157, 9.313-341, 10.937-955); Chisato (dismissal, then courtesy after the demonstration; the private disclosure; her name theory welcomed and tested, 9.152-198, 10.559-574, 10.876-921); Takina (relief when she preserves the garlic preference, appeals, the bow and embrace, siding with her dissent, 9.537-558, 10.186-231, 10.795-819, 10.905-912); Madame (a client answering for what she bought, the flick, the advice, trust on the payment, 10.684-700, 10.763-798); Mika (a cool thank-you for his assurance, 10.921-931); Mizuki (liking her driving, defending her father against her joke, 9.313-341). Not A: one day, with no peer, school or other guardian relationship, and no conversation with her father about the day. Not C: each relationship has located acts and a stated difference.

Located avowals: she would sleep badly if the guards died (9.456-479); she wanted to punish, then to frighten her father, and expected the guards to survive (10.672-709); the guards were kind and Takina might be hurt (10.728-743); the adults underestimated her (10.843-848); she dislikes her name as another of his enthusiasms (10.876-911). Not B: the story is told from others' viewpoints, and the narration withholds the hierarchy of motives behind her confession, why she delayed and whether she believes her father. Not D: her own account of her conduct is located.

Located modes with outcomes: a pointed challenge when someone presumes her tastes or speaks lightly of her father (9.250-279, 9.313-341); questioning the guards' seriousness and asking them to withdraw (9.439-479); indirect appeals while withholding the cause (10.105-231); disclosure, then public admission under pressure (10.559-656); client cancellation (10.674-714); apology addressed to the person hurt (10.795-819). Not B: the turn from appeals to disclosure is observed once and the reason for her delay is unvoiced. Not D: the modes are distinct and located with outcomes.

The row claims ethics. Located: she stipulated her own safety and counted on experienced guards surviving, deciding for people who never consented (10.672-709); she warned them they could die (9.456-479); she corrects herself that saying she never imagined this would be a bit of a lie (10.720-735); she cancels, offers the balance and reports payment (10.653-656, 10.763-798); she waits for the judgment of the particular person she hurt (10.795-819); in the car she jokes about doing a better job next time (10.865-875). Not B: her weighing is reconstructed from her retrospective account and others' readings, not shown as deliberation, and her next choice is open. Not D: located choices with stated reasons.

Located: the joke about doing a better job next time and her laugh (10.865-875); the joke about the film names she might have had as a boy (10.921-931); siding with Takina because her father knows no Latin (10.905-921). Not C: all instances fall in one car ride after the crisis and the portrait reads them only as welcoming kindness while testing it. Not E: several instances are located.

The portrait covers her whole appearance in the first story with spine-and-paragraph locators and keeps others' readings attributed: Takina's guesses about her face and motives, Madame's formulation, Mika's speculation about why she chose Madame, the narration's retreat about her credence. Not A: the row curates only this derived item, the evidence is written register only, and the After Meal retrospective belongs to Takina. Not C: her whole appearance is covered with locators.

Located bounds against overreading: no ground for ramen as her favorite dish or fine food as an abiding preference (9.340-403); no history of earlier emergencies in which her father failed to come (9.470-480); Takina's guess that she did not care about a guard is weakened by her warning (9.456-479); the appearance reading is Madame's and her nod establishes nothing about romantic interest (10.728-743); she claims no knowledge of Madame's family history (10.752-768, 10.961-975); the payment report has no receipt (10.790-798); the advance is traced to her father's account, but his authorization and the source of the cancellation transfer are open (10.384); she never had the control she claimed (10.672-709); the portrait says her responses must not be projected onto school, friendships, dating, future wrongdoing or later family routine. Not A: no forecast is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

One day, ordered by spine item and paragraph. Not B: no calendar date, her age is only estimated, the disclosure to Chisato is reported rather than transcribed, and the portrait makes no placement on the screen continuity's calendar. Not D: the within-day order and the disclosure split are precisely located.

conditions: Illustrative written Japanese only, never quotation, in the located forms: アタシ with exacting courtesy; パパ with her father present and 父 to a stranger who presumes; hesitation when she must speak at an unfamiliar counter; client language to the person she hired; たきなさん in apology (9.156-172, 9.251-265, 9.313-322, 9.543-558, 10.650-693, 10.795-814).
Interlocutors are the sampled ones: her father, Chisato, Takina, Madame, Mika, Mizuki and the 弐郎 cook.
Excluded: performed voice or timing, school peers, and any conversation with her father about the commission or the park booking.
scenario_readiness.note: The row claims speech in written register only. The located forms constrain illustrative written lines with the sampled interlocutors.

conditions: Someone presumes her tastes or speaks lightly of her father: predict a pointed, courteous-but-exacting challenge, even though she criticizes him herself (9.250-279, 9.313-341).

An unfamiliar social ritual: predict close observation of others, difficulty speaking at the decisive moment, relief and thanks when help preserves a preference she has expressed, and borrowing what works (9.491-610).
People she dismissed show competence: predict a quick revision of courtesy that still tests their seriousness (9.152-198, 9.439-479).

Before disclosure, with danger she has arranged: predict indirect appeals (call her father, abandon her, give up the work) while withholding the cause; predict disclosure when a particular person who has helped her is said to be in danger (10.105-231, 10.559-574).
Answering for harm: predict an apology addressed to the person hurt and a client's cancellation with the person she hired (10.627-819).
A kind explanation of her father's conduct: predict that she welcomes it and tests it, and meets assurances about his intentions coolly (10.876-931).
Include her mistakes: overestimating her control over hired danger, deciding for people who did not consent, withholding what would let others choose, and a self-serving account she half corrects.
Exclude a new commission or any response to her father's next absence, school, friendships, dating, guardians besides her father, a conversation with him about the day, and anything after the story.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The one day of Gluttony days' first story, split at her disclosure to Chisato: the appeals condition applies only before it, the answering-for-harm condition only after it. Her history (her mother's death, ramen and films with her father, her first visit to Japan) is background. Nothing after the story.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Her father; Chisato and Takina as guards she first dismisses and then comes to value; Madame as the professional she hired; Mika as her father's old friend; Mizuki as a driver; the cook as a stranger. A comparable new stranger who presumes her tastes is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: A first visit to Tokyo: Café LycoReco, the walk, 弐郎, Deme's home, Mizuki's car and the theme park.
No television identity, no school or home setting, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation follows the portrait's closing expectations and the located acts behind them. A new commission and her response to the next disregard are open in the portrait and are excluded.

conditions: A visitor's day as located: food choices against ready-made tourist experience, an unfamiliar counter, care for others' small needs, carsickness (9.132-157, 9.250-610, 10.69-86).
Excluded: school, hobbies, home routine and life with any guardian besides her father.
scenario_readiness.note: Her day out is well located; her ordinary life is not.

conditions: After disclosure, answering for harm she caused to a particular person: predict cancellation, payment of what she owes and an apology waiting on that person's judgment (10.653-819).
Asked to justify the commission: predict an account built on what professionals ought to withstand and on her own safety stipulation, with a partial admission when pressed (10.672-735).
Excluded: a fresh dilemma, future wrongdoing, and any claim that the day settled her conduct.
scenario_readiness.note: The row claims ethics. Her located choices support narrow answering-for-harm predictions; her weighing before the commission is known only from her retrospective account.
The portrait says nothing about romantic interest or preference follows from her nod to Madame's suggestion (10.728-743).
She has no work or school setting in the evidence. Her one engagement as a client is known chiefly from her retrospective account and is covered under cross-scenario conditions.

known_limits.statement: She names kindness and the danger to Takina; the appearance reading is Madame's and the ramen-shop theory is Takina's, and the portrait says neither gives access to her private hierarchy of motives (10.728-743).
Whether she believes her father's claim of advance planning is withheld: the narration retreats to what she made others believe, and three readings accommodate the photograph (10.937-955).

The story leaves open what she will do the next time she feels disregarded; she jokes about doing a better job and laughs when told not to, and her lasting response to Madame's advice is undisclosed (10.684-700, 10.843-875).

Her own account is of a frightening interval she would end before either guard died; Madame identifies both guards as targets, she never had that control, and she half corrects a self-serving statement (10.672-735).

The advance is traced to her father's personal account, but whether he authorized access and the source of the cancellation transfer are open; her payment report has no independent receipt (10.384, 10.790-798).
Her claim that she comes after his work is her experience; no earlier emergency in which her father failed to come is recorded (9.470-480).
Her age is only estimated, and her upbringing, her mother's background, her school, hobbies and any guardian besides her father are undisclosed (9.103-150, 9.787-801, 10.120-125).
Her portrait is confined to one story and to written register; pitch, accent and performed timing are unavailable.
Untested: her father's next absence, peers or school, a conversation with her father about the commission, and any later dealing with Madame.
